label: Siddhi-Lālasā Song One
title: kabe gaura-vane, suradhunī-taṭe
metaDescription: Siddhi-Lālasā Song One (kabe gaura-vane, suradhunī-taṭe) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.translation: When will I wander weeping under the shade of various trees and creepers on the banks of the celestial Gaṅgā river in the land of Navadvīpa, crying, “O Rādhe! O Kṛṣṇa!” and forgetting all physical comforts?

I will take my meals by begging at the homes of dog-eaters, and will drink the water of the Sarasvatī river. In ecstasy I will roll on the ground from bank to bank of the river, raising an uproar of “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!”
Bowing down to the inhabitants of the holy land, I will beg a particle of their mercy. I will smear the dust of the Vaiṣṇavas’ feet all over my body and wear the dress of a mendicant.

I will see no difference between the inhabitants of Vraja Bhūmi and those of Navadvīpa, and I will be transformed into a resident of Vraja. The true nature of the Lord’s abode will manifest itself to my eyes, and I will become a maidservant of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. *
